# Mixing Tank Upgrade: Reverse-Engineered Behavior, Findings, and Draft FDS Narrative

This is based only on the six rungs and the technician's notes. Nothing has been field-verified. Every I/O sense and every inferred behavior needs confirmation before this narrative is issued (see Open Items). Proposed tags are placeholders.

## Part A: What the legacy logic actually does

| Rung | Literal behavior | Practical effect |
|---|---|---|
| R0 | START seals in RUN_LATCH. STOP (NC) or loss of ESTOP_OK drops it. | Simple run/stop. Run status survived a power cycle in the field. |
| R1 | Fill valve opens whenever running, LSH is not made, and the fill timer is not done. | There is no "fill complete" state. Any dip below LSH reopens the fill valve, so the tank tops up continuously. |
| R2 | A retentive timer (RTO) totals all fill-valve-open time. | The timer counts *cumulative* fill time across top-ups, stops, and power cycles. It does not time a single fill. |
| R3 | The agitator runs when running and level is above LSL, **or** when the door selector is in HAND. | The HAND selector bypasses low-level protection. |
| R4 | The steam valve opens when the agitator *output* is on and TEMP_LOW is made. | The steam interlock depends on the agitator command, not on proof that it runs. Through HAND, steam can flow into a near-empty tank. |
| R5 | The horn sounds on fill timeout only. | There is one alarm, with no acknowledge or silence. |
| R6 | START resets the fill timer. | Pressing START clears the timeout and restarts the fill, with no diagnosis. |

The process is never drained or discharged in this logic. Either withdrawal happens downstream, outside this PLC, or it is manual. This determines whether the upgrade is an ISA-106 continuous module or an ISA-88 batch unit (OI-01).

## Part B: Behaviors not to carry forward

| ID | Location | Issue | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| F-01 | R0, tech note | **The unit auto-restarted on power restore and began filling unattended.** The export shows a seal-in, but the observed behavior means either the real instruction is OTL/latched, retained data is involved, or the export is incomplete. | Power restore always enters STOPPED with all outputs off. Require an operator START (FR-MIX-030). Check the actual SLC rung type before decommissioning so you understand the root cause. |
| F-02 | R0 | E-stop is only a PLC input in the run latch. If the PLC fails, the E-stop does nothing. | Hardwire the E-stop through a safety relay that removes output power. The PLC only monitors it. Set the category by risk assessment, and put any SIF in the SRS. |
| F-03 | R3 | **The AGIT_HAND door selector defeats the low-level interlock.** The agitator can run dry and damage the seal or gearbox. | Remove the bypass. If maintenance needs a bump, provide a managed HMI maintenance mode with authorization, a time limit, and a log entry. |
| F-04 | R3 + R4 | Through HAND, steam can be admitted with level below LSL. This risks coil exposure, scorching, and local overheating. | Steam permissive = level above LSL **and** agitator run proven. The permissive must not be bypassable (C&E chart). |
| F-05 | R4 | The steam interlock uses the agitator output bit, not run feedback. A tripped overload still allows steam. | Add a motor auxiliary or run contact. Interlock steam to proven run. |
| F-06 | R4 | There is no high-temperature protection. If TEMP_LOW sticks ON, steam stays open indefinitely. | Add an independent TSH or TT high trip. Evaluate it as a possible SIF (OI-05). |
| F-07 | R1 | LSH failure direction is unknown. If it is energized-on-high, a broken wire reads "not high" and the tank overflows. | Wire LSH fail-safe (de-energized = high), or use a line-monitored input. Add an LSH/LSL discrepancy check. |
| F-08 | R1 | Fill reopens on any dip below LSH. This causes valve cycling on splash or vortexing and hides real leaks. | Define a discrete fill step that ends on LSH with a debounce. Top-up, if needed at all, uses a defined condition (OI-02). |
| F-09 | R2 | The RTO totals fill time across cycles and power loss. Normal top-ups eventually cause a false timeout. A slow real fault can be masked by earlier resets. | Use a non-retentive timer per fill step. It resets at each fill-step entry. |
| F-10 | R6 | START clears the timeout and resumes filling. A stuck or failed fill gets "fixed" by pushing START. | Separate ACK (alarm), RESET (fault), and START (run command). Block START while a fault is active. |
| F-11 | R1, R5 | On fill timeout, only the fill valve closes. Agitator and steam keep running and the unit stays "running". | Fill timeout puts the unit in HELD with defined output states. |
| F-12 | R5 | One horn, no ack or silence, no alarm for agitator fail, high temp, or instrument fault. | Rationalize alarms per ISA-18.2 and reference the alarm database. |
| F-13 | All | The fill and steam valves have no position feedback, so a stuck-open valve is undetectable. | Add closed limit switches on XV-101 and XV-102, or accept the risk and record it (OI-06). |
| F-14 | R4 | Temperature is controlled on/off from a switch. There is no visible deadband and no PV for trending. | Prefer a TT with on/off or PID control. If the switch stays, add minimum on/off times from the setpoint list. |

The highest priorities are **F-01, F-02, F-03/F-04, and F-07**. Treat them as safety findings, and route them through your PHA/risk assessment, not just the FDS review.

## Part C: Draft functional narrative

### Mixing Tank TK-101 — Control Narrative (FDS Section X), Rev A (Draft)

#### 1. Purpose and boundaries

TK-101 receives liquid through XV-101. It mixes the contents with agitator M-101 and heats them with steam through XV-102.

- Upstream: fill supply to XV-101 (source TBD, OI-03).
- Downstream: withdrawal method TBD (OI-01).
- Utilities: steam supply to XV-102.
- Out of scope: E-stop safety function (hardwired, see §6) and any SIF (see SRS, OI-05).

#### 2. Equipment and tags

Refer to the instrument index for ranges, wiring sense, and fail positions. The placeholder tags used here, mapped to the legacy points:

| Proposed tag | Legacy point | Function |
|---|---|---|
| HS-101A | I:1/0 | START |
| HS-101B | I:1/1 | STOP (NC) |
| XS-101 | I:1/2 | E-stop healthy (monitor only) |
| LSL-101 | I:1/3 | Level above low point |
| LSH-101 | I:1/4 | Level high |
| HS-102 | I:1/5 | Legacy HAND selector, to be removed (F-03) |
| TSL-101 | I:1/6 | Temperature low |
| XV-101 | O:2/0 | Fill valve |
| M-101 | O:2/1 | Agitator |
| XV-102 | O:2/2 | Steam valve |
| YA-101 | O:2/3 | Horn |
| M-101 run feedback | New | Agitator proven run (F-05) |

#### 3. States and transitions (ISA-106)

| State | Outputs | Entry permissives | Initiator | Allowed exits | Automation level |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| STOPPED | XV-101 closed, M-101 off, XV-102 closed | None. This is the default state on power-up, STOP, E-stop, or comms loss. | Auto / operator | → STARTING | Operator-prompted |
| STARTING | Start sequence §5.1 | E-stop healthy, no active fault, LSH/LSL consistent, operator START | Operator | → RUNNING, → HELD, → STOPPED | Automatic |
| RUNNING | XV-101 closed, M-101 on, temperature control active | Start sequence complete | Auto | → HELD, → STOPPED | Automatic |
| HELD | XV-101 closed, XV-102 closed; M-101 per C&E chart | Any fault in §5.1 or §8 | Auto | → STOPPED (STOP), → STARTING (RESET then START) | Operator-prompted |

- FR-MIX-001: The unit shall enter STOPPED on power-up, with all outputs de-energized. *Test: cycle power in each state and verify STOPPED.*
- FR-MIX-002: The unit shall reject START while any entry permissive for STARTING is not met. The HMI shall show the missing permissive. *Test: defeat each permissive in turn and push START.*
- FR-MIX-003: STOP shall move the unit to STOPPED from any state. *Test: push STOP in each state.*
- FR-MIX-004: The unit shall leave HELD only through STOP, or through RESET followed by START. *Test: try START without RESET in HELD; verify rejection.*
- FR-MIX-005: Operations shall approve this state table before IFC. *Test: signed review record.*

#### 4. Regulatory control

**Temperature (TSL-101 → XV-102), on/off.**
- PV: TSL-101. Output: XV-102. Action: open on low temperature.
- Active only in RUNNING, and in STARTING after step S3. Closed in all other states.
- XV-102 respects the minimum on-time and off-time in the setpoint list.
- FR-MIX-010: XV-102 shall open only when TSL-101 is active and the steam permissive in the C&E chart is met. *Test: simulate TSL-101 with each permissive true and false.*
- FR-MIX-011: XV-102 shall not change state faster than the minimum on/off times in the setpoint list. *Test: toggle TSL-101 rapidly and record XV-102 timing.*

If a TT replaces TSL-101 (OI-04), revise this section for PV, mode behavior, and bad-PV response.

#### 5. Sequences

##### 5.1 Start sequence (SqBC, STARTING state)

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | Check permissives. | All STARTING permissives met. | None (evaluated once) | Reject START. Stay in STOPPED. Show missing permissive. |
| S2 | Open XV-101. Start the fill timer. | LSL-101 active for the debounce time. | Fill timeout (setpoint list), timed from S2 entry | Close XV-101. Go to HELD. Raise fill-timeout alarm. |
| S3 | Start M-101. | M-101 run feedback active. | Agitator start timeout (setpoint list) | Stop M-101. Close XV-101. Go to HELD. Raise agitator-fail alarm. |
| S4 | Enable temperature control. Keep XV-101 open. | LSH-101 active for the debounce time. | Fill timeout (continues from S2) | Close XV-101 and XV-102. Go to HELD. Raise fill-timeout alarm. |
| S5 | Close XV-101. Stop the fill timer. Enter RUNNING. | XV-101 closed (no position feedback; command only, OI-06). | N/A until OI-06 is closed | N/A |

If LSH-101 is already active at S1, the sequence goes to S3 and skips the fill.

- FR-MIX-020: The fill timer shall reset at each S2 entry and shall not retain its value through STOP, HELD, or power loss. *Test: interrupt a fill, restart it, and verify the timer starts from zero.*
- FR-MIX-021: Each step in §5.1 shall run its failure response when its timeout expires. *Test: inhibit each transition condition and verify the response.*
- FR-MIX-022: In RUNNING, XV-101 shall stay closed when LSH-101 clears, until OI-02 defines top-up. *Test: clear LSH-101 in RUNNING and verify XV-101 stays closed.*

#### 6. Interlocks and permissives

Refer to the cause-and-effect chart CE-MIX-101 (to be issued, OI-07). Minimum causes to include:

- E-stop not healthy
- LSL-101 inactive (agitator and steam)
- M-101 not proven (steam)
- LSH-101/LSL-101 discrepancy
- High temperature (new instrument)

The E-stop is a hardwired safety function. The PLC monitors XS-101 only.

- FR-MIX-025: No BPCS interlock shall have a field or panel bypass. Bypasses shall be possible only through the managed bypass function in the control philosophy. *Test: inspect the panel, then try a bypass without authorization.*
- FR-MIX-026: Each cause in CE-MIX-101 shall produce each listed effect. *Test: execute CE-MIX-101 line by line at FAT.*

#### 7. Alarms

Refer to the rationalized alarm database, entries ALM-MIX-101-xx. Candidates for rationalization: fill timeout, agitator fail to start, agitator stopped while running, level instrument discrepancy, high temperature, E-stop active.

- FR-MIX-030: YA-101 shall silence on operator ACK. ACK shall not reset a fault or start the unit. *Test: raise an alarm, push ACK, and verify state and outputs do not change.*

#### 8. Abnormal handling

| Condition | Response |
|---|---|
| Bad PV: LSH-101 and LSL-101 inconsistent (high made, low not made) | Go to HELD. Raise the discrepancy alarm. |
| Bad PV: TSL-101 | Cannot be detected with a switch. See OI-04. |
| LSL-101 clears in RUNNING | Stop M-101. Close XV-102. Go to HELD. |
| M-101 run feedback lost in RUNNING | Close XV-102. Go to HELD. |
| I/O comms loss | Outputs go to their de-energized state. Unit goes to STOPPED on recovery. |
| HMI comms loss | The unit stays in its current state. Panel STOP and E-stop stay functional. |
| Power loss and restart | Enter STOPPED. Hold all outputs off until operator START (FR-MIX-001). |
| Fail positions | XV-101 fail-closed, XV-102 fail-closed, M-101 stops (confirm, OI-06). |

- FR-MIX-040: Each condition in the §8 table shall produce its listed response. *Test: simulate each condition at FAT.*

#### 9. Operator interface

The operator sees:
- Unit state
- Current step
- Fill timer elapsed and limit
- Status of LSL-101, LSH-101, TSL-101, and M-101 run
- Commanded state of XV-101 and XV-102
- Missing permissives
- Active faults

The operator can push START, STOP, RESET, and ACK.

Prompts:
- In STOPPED after power-up: "Power restored. Make sure that the tank is safe to start. Push START."
- In HELD: "Unit held. Find and correct the cause. Push RESET, then push START."

- FR-MIX-050: Operations shall approve all prompt text before FAT. *Test: signed review record.*

#### 10. Setpoint list (draft, values to be confirmed)

| Item | Legacy value | Proposed | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fill timeout | 600 s (cumulative RTO) | TBD from measured fill rate | Process |
| LSL/LSH debounce | None | TBD | Controls |
| Agitator start timeout | None | TBD | Controls |
| XV-102 minimum on/off time | None | TBD | Process |

#### 11. Open items

| ID | Item | Owner | Due |
|---|---|---|---|
| OI-01 | Confirm the process: continuous (ISA-106) or batch with discharge (ISA-88). Identify the withdrawal method. | Process lead | TBD |
| OI-02 | Decide whether RUNNING needs top-up and on what condition. Consider adding an LT. | Process lead | TBD |
| OI-03 | Identify the fill source and any upstream permissive. | Process lead | TBD |
| OI-04 | Replace TSL-101 with a TT? Add a TSH. | Process / I&C | TBD |
| OI-05 | PHA/LOPA for overflow, dry-run, and overheat. Move any SIF to the SRS. | Safety lead | TBD |
| OI-06 | Field-verify all I/O wiring sense and valve fail positions. Decide on valve limit switches. | I&C tech | TBD |
| OI-07 | Issue CE-MIX-101. | Controls lead | TBD |
| OI-08 | Find the root cause of the legacy power-restart behavior (rung type, retained data). | Controls lead | Before SLC removal |
| OI-09 | Assign final tag numbers to replace the placeholders. | I&C lead | TBD |

Owners and dates are placeholders. I can't assign them from the export, so fill them in at the review meeting.
